chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who withholds the zakat will ask for return at the time of death,'
and this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'My Lord, send me back, that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who withholds zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) linking the specific penalty for withholding zakat to the Quranic concept of 'Barzakh' (the intermediate realm). The Imam interprets the plea 'Rabb irjiʿun' (My Lord, send me back) not merely as a general post-mortem desire, but as the distinct supplication of the zakat-withholder, highlighting a unique eschatological consequence in Shia tradition. This connects the ritual obligation of wealth purification directly to the soul's state during the interval between death and resurrection.
